steps.message: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: The spend report books each exported usage line against its first attribution code even when that code passes the cost through a chain to another owner. Produce one row for every code that ultimately carries spend, with its metered quantity, money and contributing line count. Place every amount under exactly one final code rather than an intermediate code. If a chain repeats, use the charge code shared by that cycle. The onboarding record in the metering bucket identifies readable accounts and the locations of exports and attribution material. This task includes a local AWS-compatible emulator at the preconfigured AWS_ENDPOINT_URL. Its credentials and region are already in the shell, the repository's AWS SDK clients use it, and no real AWS account is involved. You may inspect its resources while developing and testing.

| .prettierrc.json - prettier formatting file  
| .eslintrc.cjs - linter configuration only comment out linting rules if there a good reason  
| .gitignore - ignored files for source control  
| src - source for the api application  


# Getting started with Local Development

# Environment

-   Latest version of [NVM](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm)
-   Latest version of NodeJS 18.x `nvm install 18`
-   Latest version of [AWS CLI](https://aws.amazon.com/cli/)
-   Latest version of [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/)
-   Assigned AWS accounts and IAM credentials
-   [Redoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc#redoc-cli) for automatically generating html from the open api specification, see install [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25800493/converting-swagger-specification-json-to-html-documentation)
-   Latest version of [Kind](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/) for the local integration test enviornment, see install [here](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/docs/user/quick-start/#installation)
-   Latest version of [Helm](https://helm.sh/) see the install guild [here](https://helm.sh/docs/intro/install/)

For the remainng item of this list, you should figure out yourself if you don't already know.

-   [Git](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Getting-Started-Installing-Git)
-   A good terminal (such as [iTerm2](https://iterm2.com/index.html) + [ohmyzsh](https://ohmyz.sh/))
-   A good IDE (such as [VSCode](https://code.visualstudio.com/), or [WebStorm](https://www.jetbrains.com/webstorm/))
-   Helpful for command line navigation [z](https://facilecode.com/how-to-setup-z-jump-around/)

# Setup

1. Configure AWS CLI. `aws configure`. See sample config below. Use _us-east-1_ as default region and _json_ as default output format.

```bash
aws configure
AWS Access Key ID [None]: XXXXXXXXXXX
AWS Secret Access Key [None]: XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
Default region name [None]: us-east-1
Default output format [None]: json
```

2. Clone the repository.
3. Run: `npm run setup:influx` Visit _http://localhost:8086_ to make sure InfluxDB is running locally.
4. Going through the setup guide of local InfuxDB. Configure the `local-usage-data` bucket, the `local-config` bucket and the `paigo` org. **Case sensitive**.
5. [Get an API Token from the Influx instance](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/cloud/security/tokens/create-token/)
6. Create the following file at the root directory of the project named `.env`, where the `INFLUX_URL`, `INFLUX_TOKEN` and `INFLUX_ORG` values are stored

Your token will be different than the one below.

steps.message:
All changes are complete and verified. Summary of the fix:

**Problem**: The spend report booked each exported usage line under the first charge code its attribution reference named, even when that material passes the cost through to another owner.

**Changes**

1. `src/onboarding/entities/attributionDirectory.entity.ts` — now a chain resolver rather than a single lookup. It follows every hand-off until the code that finally carries spend:
   - `pool/x` → pool document (`rollsUpTo`)
   - `unit/x` → `attribution/units/x.json` (`parentRef`)
   - `alias/x` → SSM parameter `/paigo/attribution/alias/x`
   - `node/<account>/<region>/<instance>` → EC2 tags `paigoChargeCode` / `paigoRollsInto`, read with the owning account's assumed-role credentials
   - Cycles settle on the charge code the cycle shares; unreadable material leaves the spend on the last code the chain named; hops are cached so each reference is read once.
2. `src/onboarding/entities/meteringAccounts.entity.ts` — the onboarding record loads as a real instance and hands out per-account credentials (`credentialsForAccountId`), so node hops are read in the account/region that owns them and stop cleanly for accounts the record doesn't list.
3. `src/microservices/usageAttribution/usageAttribution.service.ts` — every line is resolved to its final code and booked there exactly once.
4. `src/utils/aws/awsSSM.ts` / `awsEc2.ts` — added tolerant `getParameterValue` and `getInstanceTags` helpers.
5. Added `usageAttribution.service.spec.ts` covering direct pools, pass-through chains, mixed unit/alias/node/pool chains, repeating chains, unreadable hops, unknown references and single-count aggregation.

**Live emulator result**: 16 rows (was 16 wrong codes before, now the ultimate owners e.g. `cc-warehouse-etl`, `cc-identity-svc`, `cc-content-index`, `cc-batch-scoring`), preserving all 33 lines, quantity 5043 and amount 1335.41, with each amount under exactly one final code. Full unit suite passes (294 tests).
